subject: Excel
text: StartDateTime is written month-first (for example 7/18/2016 6:00). Explain what goes wrong if your computer uses Danish regional settings, and how you import the column so the dates are right.

method: In Power Query, right-click the column > Change Type > Using Locale > Date/Time, English (United States). In the legacy Text Import Wizard, set the column data format to Date: MDY. Check afterwards that the column is right-aligned and that no month exceeds 12.

subject: Excel
text: PreparerID 101 appears five times in PreparerInfo. Explain why a lookup on PreparerID alone gives wrong names, and what the correct key is.
answer: PreparerID is only unique within a business unit: ID 101 is a different person in each of five units. The unique key is PreparerID together with BusinessUnitID. A lookup on PreparerID alone returns the first match (Carolyn Slater) for all 278 lines with ID 101.
method: Build a helper key in both tables, for example =D2&"-"&C2, and look up on that; or use XLOOKUP with two conditions: =XLOOKUP(1,(PreparerInfo!B:B=D2)*(PreparerInfo!C:C=C2),PreparerInfo!A:A).

subject: Excel
text: Using the composite key PreparerID + BusinessUnitID, attach PreparerName to every journal entry line. Which preparer has the most lines?
answer: Carolyn Slater with 182 lines; Elizabeth Rees is next with 158.
method: Helper key in both sheets (=PreparerID&"-"&BusinessUnitID), XLOOKUP on the helper, then a PivotTable counting lines per preparer.

subject: Excel
text: PreparerName holds values such as "Carolyn Slater|Food Operations Manager" followed by invisible padding. How do you separate the name from the job title and remove the padding?
answer: Split on the pipe: the name is the text before | and the title is the text after it. The padding is non-breaking spaces (character 160), which TRIM alone does not remove. 10 of the 12 entries contain a pipe; the others (POS, GUESTSYS) are systems, not people.
method: Name =LEFT(A2,FIND("|",A2)-1); title =TRIM(SUBSTITUTE(MID(A2,FIND("|",A2)+1,99),CHAR(160),"")). Wrap in IFERROR for the entries with no pipe.

subject: Excel
text: When you import the job codes file, the codes 001 to 012 turn into 1 to 12. Why does that matter for this case, and how do you stop it?
answer: Excel converts them to numbers and drops the leading zeros. The case states job codes are three-digit text, and the code you extract from the Job field (for example 005) is text, so a lookup of "005" against the number 5 fails.
method: Set the column's data type to Text during import (Power Query: Change Type > Text; wizard: column data format Text). To repair afterwards use =TEXT(A2,"000").
